errors.why: In this ritual context རང་མཚན means one's own name (the practitioner states his name before 'I, Vajra...'), not the epistemological 'self-characteristic' (svalakṣaṇa).

errors.english: the sign of the first action and of slightly coming under the power of primordial wisdom
errors.why: ལས་དང་པོ here names the beginner (ādikarmika) stage of yogin, paired with one who has slight mastery of wisdom, not 'the first action'.

note: A close, competent rendering of the maṇḍala and consort-practice commentary; one ritual term (own name) misread as a philosophical one.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the beautiful liberation and the four formless liberations.
Faithful word-commentary on the wrathful iconography and Vajrapāṇi's proclamation; the sentence on vajra-flame weapons is clumsy but not wrong in substance.
Faithful rendering of the lamp-and-darkness simile and the verses on the deity's form and nirvāṇa.

errors.english: [note: The text continues with a commentary on the Vajravarahi Tantra]
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'by me' and so forth refers to Vajravārāhī (as the hearer); the text is still the Ḍākārṇava commentary, not a commentary on a Vajravārāhī Tantra, and that clause is left untranslated.

fix.find: The Blessed One is the teacher... [note: The text continues with a commentary on the Vajravarahi Tantra]
fix.replace: The Blessed One is the teacher; "by me" and so forth refers to Vajravārāhī's...

errors.english: For wrathful activities, burn a corpse.
errors.why: The verse lists styluses; for abhicāra the implement is one from (charred wood of) a cremated corpse, not an instruction to burn a corpse.

note: Accurate on the long verse lists of styluses, surfaces, vessels and rosaries and on the caṇḍālī verses; the closing note misidentifies the text.

errors.english: Undoubtedly, the nature of reality is not exactly like that.
errors.why: The Tibetan affirms: undoubtedly it is just so, since ultimate and conventional exist in mutual dependence.

fix.find: Undoubtedly, the nature of reality is not exactly like that.

errors.english: If the logic of understanding the twelve (ayatana) sense spheres is the same across the board
errors.why: The objection is that, by that reasoning, impermanence etc. apply equally to all twelve āyatanas, so why does the sūtra include them in the dharmāyatana alone; 'logic of understanding the twelve sense spheres' garbles the argument.

note: The analysis of individual and general characteristics of the kleśas is sound, but the opening sentence is reversed and the closing Abhidharma objection is muddled.

errors.english: someone might attain the first meditative concentration [note: Sanskrit: "dhyana"]. When they attain the second meditative concentration, and so on up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, because they have not experienced those specific objects,
errors.why: One who has attained the first dhyāna, not having experienced the domain of those who attain the second dhyāna up to the summit, takes the first dhyāna for arhatship; the English has him attaining the higher states.

fix.find: someone might attain the first meditative concentration [note: Sanskrit: "dhyana"]. When they attain the second meditative concentration, and so on up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, because they have not experienced those specific objects,
fix.replace: one who has attained the first meditative concentration [note: Sanskrit: "dhyana"], because they have not experienced the domain of those who attain the second meditative concentration and so on up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,

errors.english: it is said in the texts of the Vaisheshika [note: a non-Buddhist school of Indian philosophy]
errors.why: In this Abhidharma/Vinaya context the source analysing the origin of the view that there are no arhats is the Vibhāṣā (Vaibhāṣika treatise), not Vaiśeṣika texts.

errors.english: I know nothing other than this existence
errors.why: The arhat formula (nāparam itthatvāt) means 'I know no further existence beyond this one', not that one knows nothing other than this existence.

note: The four-truths mapping and the logicians' view are rendered well, but the meditators' case is mis-segmented and the arhat formula is rendered misleadingly throughout.

errors.english: the ritual characteristics of the bali and the mandala offerings
errors.why: འཁོར་ལོ་མཆོད་པ is the circle worship (cakrapūjā / gaṇacakra), not maṇḍala offerings.

errors.english: Through gestures, all defining characteristics are perfectly completed.
errors.why: In this list of offerings ཕྱག is homage/prostration (followed by joined palms), not hand gestures in general.

note: A sound rendering of the offering verses, colophon and the opening of the chapter on laying out the maṇḍala, with two minor ritual-term slips.

errors.english: release the ends and so forth
errors.why: མཐའ་མ in a mudrā description is the little finger; the little fingers etc. are released, not 'the ends'.

note: Careful and accurate description of the consecration mudrās and the Paramādya commentary colophon.

errors.english: Because it is difficult and involves suffering, one must have great faith
errors.why: The gloss explains the sūtra's 'hard to have faith in': conviction in it is difficult and painful, so it is hard to believe, not that one must have great faith.

errors.english: The Perfection of Wisdom is not something to be exerted upon
errors.why: The sūtra lemma says the Perfection of Wisdom is hard to believe for one who has not exerted himself (anabhiyukta), not that it is not to be exerted upon.

errors.english: to claim that this [note: inconsistency] is the definition
errors.why: 'This' is the proposed criterion of the Buddha's Word, which fails to pervade; the note 'inconsistency' misidentifies the referent.

note: Solid on the four causes of abandoning the Dharma and the chapter colophon; the transition into chapter eight misreads the sūtra lemma and its gloss.
